# A gate run does not notice its own binary is older than the base ref it pins

`review-plan` (and every other code-reading gate) snapshots the base ref's tree into
`/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots/<sha>/` and reviews against it, but nothing compares the
RUNNING BUILD to that sha. A checkout that has drifted behind `origin/main` silently
reviews new material with old code.

## Observed

Three consecutive `review-plan` runs were executed from `~/rebar/.venv` — a legitimate
repo checkout venv, which is what AGENTS.md asks for — while that checkout sat 24 commits
behind `origin/main`. The only symptom was one easily-missed line:

    WARNING rebar.config: rebar config (/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots/2bce1407.../rebar.toml):
    unknown key 'verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets' ignored (typo? see docs/config.md)

That key is not a typo. Commit 74a7332606 ("9416: rename overlap_enabled for what it
does") renamed `verify.overlap_enabled` -> `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`. The stale
build predates the rename, so it read the CURRENT base ref's config, did not recognise the
current key name, and silently ignored the operator's setting.

## Scope

Operator decision (2026-08-12): this ticket covers the build-drift warning only. The
fourth criterion of the original report — surfacing repeated non-fatal LLM step failures
in run summaries — is split out to `eclectic-industrial-argali` (61a1-ee49-3c42-4b09),
linked `discovered_from`.

## Design

All code-reading gates converge on `rebar.llm.gate_source.resolve_gate_handle`, which
resolves the base ref to a pinned sha and acquires the snapshot handle. That is the one
seam where a drift check belongs.

The running build's commit is already resolvable: `rebar.signing._gate_commit_sha()`
returns the live rebar source checkout's short sha, falling back to the build-baked
`rebar._build_info.COMMIT` (written by `hatch_build.py`) for wheel installs, and `None`
when neither exists.

Drift = the running build's commit is a strict ancestor of the pinned sha, measured in
the target repo. When the gate code and the target repo are different repositories the
build sha simply is not present in the target repo, so the check finds nothing and stays
silent — which is the correct behaviour, since drift is only meaningful when rebar is
reviewing rebar.

The warning is advisory: reviewing from a slightly-behind checkout is legitimate, so this
must never fail a run, never alter a verdict, and never change signing or provenance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — When the running build's commit is a strict ancestor of the sha a gate pins,
      the gate emits ONE warning naming the build sha, the build commit's date, the pinned
      sha, and the drift count in commits. It does NOT fail and does NOT alter the verdict,
      exit code, signature, or provenance stamp.
- [ ] AC2 — The warning is emitted at most once per (build sha, pinned sha) pair per
      process, so a run that resolves the handle more than once does not produce a warning
      storm.
- [ ] AC3 — When build provenance is unavailable or drift cannot be established, the gate
      is SILENT: no warning when `_gate_commit_sha()` returns `None`, when the build sha is
      not present in the target repo (gate code and target are different repos), when the
      pinned sha is unknown, when git is unavailable, or when the build is at or ahead of
      the pinned sha.
- [ ] AC4 — An unknown key in a config snapshot is reported differently when the running
      build is known to be behind the pinned ref: 'unknown key X (this build may predate
      it; see docs/config.md)' instead of the 'typo?' wording, which actively misdirects.
      The default wording is unchanged when no drift was detected.
- [ ] AC5 — Held-out unit tests cover: behind -> warns once; at/ahead -> silent; provenance
      unavailable -> silent; build sha absent from the target repo -> silent; and the
      config unknown-key wording in both the drifted and undrifted states.
- [ ] AC6 — `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the unit + interfaces suites pass; every
      touched file stays under the 800-LOC module cap.

## Provenance

Found while re-running plan review for task b2bb during the store/signing remediation.
Re-running from a worktree venv at origin/main is the workaround.
